title: Sirius Passet Lagerstätte (North Greenland)
summary: Sirius Passet is a remote fossil site in Peary Land, northern Greenland, found by chance in 1984. Its dark mudstones preserve soft parts of early Cambrian animals, mostly arthropods, from low-oxygen seas. It is among the oldest exceptionally preserved faunas from the Cambrian explosion.

uncertainty.note: Stage 3 of the Cambrian is given as 521-514 Ma by Park et al. (2019); the exact age of the fauna within the stage is not fixed by the sources opened. Paleo-position is computed at 517.5 Ma, the stage midpoint.

as_recorded.value: equated with Stage 3 of the Cambrian Period (521–514 Ma)

when.display: Early Cambrian, Stage 3 (521–514 million years ago)

where.modern_name: Sirius Passet, Peary Land, North Greenland
where.historical_name: Slope setting at the edge of the Portfjeld carbonate platform on the Laurentian margin, early Cambrian; no polities exist at this date

importance.justification: One of the oldest Cambrian Lagerstätten, showing soft-bodied animals early in the Cambrian explosion.
